title: California Wildfires and the Truth Behind Religious Claims
description:
When tragedy strikes — like the recent Los Angeles wildfires that killed 24 people — some believers rush to declare it “God’s punishment.” A viral reel even claimed the disaster happened because LA was “godless.” But does this claim hold up?

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts debunks the idea that natural disasters are divine punishment. From the Great Flood myths to Sodom and Gomorrah in the Bible, from Zeus’s storms to Hindu gods of cosmic balance, ancient cultures invented these stories to explain nature. But today we know the science: wildfires are caused by climate change, high temperatures, and ignition sources — not angry gods

We revisit tragedies at deeply religious sites — the Kedarnath floods (2013), the Chamoli earthquake (1999), stampedes at Sabarimala and Kumbh Mela, even Mecca’s crane collapse (2015) and Hajj stampede (2,400 dead) — and ask: if disasters are punishment, why do they strike sacred places? From the 2004 tsunami hitting Indonesia’s Muslim majority to the Iran Bam earthquake (26,000 dead), disasters show no religious bias.

Believers suffer from confirmation bias and apophenia, seeing divine “control” where randomness and science explain the cause. Worse, some rejoice when people of another religion die in disasters — forgetting humanity itself. If you’ve searched for is God in control, divine punishment debunked, natural disasters explained, why do disasters happen, or religion and disasters, this video gives you the rational perspective.

#GodNotInControl #ScienceOverSuperstition #CriticalThinking #NaturalDisastersExplained #BlindFaith
